clue.text: Insect observed to rise over head of prey

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: observed means saw

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A creature is spotted climbing above its victim before striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns SAW upwards to WAS, and 'head of' gives the P of 'prey' beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: The stinging yellow-and-black flier is a familiar kind of insect.

clue.text: Source of help obliterating one experience

indicators.note: the source of help wipes out the following item, so that letter is struck from it

parts.note: a saviour is someone who comes to your rescue
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A helper wipes out a person's memory of something they went through.
explanation.definitionFit: To savour something is to taste or undergo it fully, a verb sense matching experience.

clue.text: Gather lab seems in a mess

indicators.note: things in a mess are jumbled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone tidying a cluttered laboratory says it looks chaotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges the letters of LAB and SEEMS.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather people or things is to bring them together, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Kitchen tools, say, supported by this country's consumers

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of what follows, held up by it

parts.note: say introduces an example, abbreviated eg
GB, Great Britain, is this country for a British paper
consumers of food are eaters

explanation.surface: Britain's shoppers are said to be propping up sales of kitchen gadgets.
explanation.definitionFit: Whisks for beating eggs are utensils found in any cooking area.

clue.text: Article sometimes partly sent up

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters are read upwards
partly says only a portion of the word is used

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece occasionally mocks its subject.
explanation.walkthrough: 'partly' picks METI from inside 'sometimes', and 'sent up' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An item is a single piece in a newspaper, an article.

clue.text: Spice drink, source of disease mostly

parts.note: gin is a spirit, a drink

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the word is used

parts.note: a germ is a microbe that causes illness

explanation.surface: A spiced drink is blamed for spreading illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts the last letter from GERM.
explanation.definitionFit: The knobbly root is ground into a hot, aromatic seasoning.

clue.text: Teacher raced out into different form

indicators.note: putting letters into a different form means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A schoolmaster dashed out to change into another class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'into different form' rearranges RACED OUT; 'form' also suggests a school class.
explanation.definitionFit: An educator is one who instructs, a synonym of teacher.

clue.text: Dawn chorus, in Baroque style?

parts.note: birdsong at daybreak is music sung at an early hour, while Baroque compositions belong to the period-instrument repertoire of centuries past

explanation.surface: Birds at sunrise sound as ornate as a Bach suite.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names Medieval to Baroque repertoire, and literally the songbirds' first-light singing.

clue.text: Novel extract prepared for the Asian market?

definitions.meaning: a book by E M Forster

definitions.text: extract prepared for the Asian market?
definitions.meaning: an extract is a passage, and something bound for the Asian market is going to India

explanation.definitionFit: Forster's book title; read literally it is a piece of text heading to the subcontinent.

clue.text: Saying publicity work's finished with book

parts.note: publicity work is PR, public relations; the 's stands for is, a link
finished means over

explanation.surface: A press officer announces a campaign is complete and a book is out.
explanation.definitionFit: A proverb is a short traditional maxim, a saying.

clue.text: Misrepresented a claim about Government? Wonderful

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters are placed around the next piece
a claim misrepresented is distorted, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone twisted a statement about the Government, and it went down marvellously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Misrepresented' rearranges A CLAIM, and 'about' wraps those letters around G.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enchanting or marvellous is called magical, a synonym of wonderful.

clue.text: Teenage heart's response over boyband, primarily

definitions.text: Teenage heart's response over boyband, primarily

indicators.note: primarily means the first letters of the words are taken

explanation.surface: A teenager's pulse races at the sight of a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'primarily' takes the first letter of each of the five words before it; the whole clue also describes a pounding pulse, as in a heart-throb.
explanation.definitionFit: A throb is the pounding of a heart excited by a pop idol.

clue.text: It's the preserve of motorists

parts.note: a preserve reads as a domain kept for one group, but it is also a fruit spread, here one made by stationary cars

explanation.surface: Something reserved for drivers alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A long queue of stuck vehicles is a kind of 'jam' that only drivers make.

clue.text: Dreary task linked to top of trees in a curious tree plantation

indicators.note: in means the first pieces are placed inside the following pair

parts.note: rum is a British word for odd or curious
a bore is a tedious thing to do

indicators.note: top of means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A dull job attached to the treetops in an odd plantation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the dull job and the T from 'top of' inside the pair from 'a curious'; 'rum' for strange is British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An arboretum is a botanical garden planted with many species of trees.

clue.text: More overt style? Nonsense

parts.note: balder, more bald, means plainer or more blunt
dash means flair or style

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a more direct manner of speaking as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is senseless talk, a synonym of nonsense.

clue.text: Novel about the Venus de Milo?

definitions.meaning: the famous statue has lost both its upper limbs, so a story about it would say goodbye to them

explanation.definitionFit: Hemingway's war book title; read literally it is a goodbye to limbs, which the statue lacks.

clue.text: A besieged city invaded by 100 — it's a cruel act

indicators.note: invaded by means the following pieces go inside the city

parts.note: Troy was besieged by the Greeks for ten years
C is the Roman numeral for 100
it is taken as written; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: A sieged town is overrun by a hundred troops, which is a brutal deed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invaded by' puts the hundred and 'it' inside the city the Greeks besieged, after the opening A.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrocity is a wicked or brutal deed.

clue.text: Whales and I at sea around Scottish islands

parts.note: orca, killer whale, can be a plural like sheep

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone out on the water watches whales near some northern islands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges 'and I' into DIAN; the orca's plural can be the same as its singular.
explanation.definitionFit: Orcadian describes a person or thing from Orkney, the islands off northern Scotland.

clue.text: Treats foe roughly — evidence of what's to come?

indicators.note: treated roughly, the letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone manhandles an enemy as a warning of worse to follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A foretaste is an early sample hinting at what lies ahead.

clue.text: Kerfuffle about the French weapons centre

indicators.note: about means the fuss word goes around the next piece

parts.note: a to-do is a commotion or fuss
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A fuss breaks out over a French arms factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the fuss around the French article; a kerfuffle is British slang for a commotion.
explanation.definitionFit: The Spanish city has been famed for sword-making for centuries.

clue.text: Funny man in company glued to the microphone

indicators.note: glued to means the first piece is stuck directly onto the next

parts.note: mic is short for microphone

explanation.surface: A comedian in a troupe never lets go of the microphone.
explanation.definitionFit: A comic is a comedian, someone who makes people laugh.

clue.text: Consider injecting chlorine for strength

indicators.note: injecting means the next piece is put inside the first

parts.note: to muse is to ponder or consider
Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine

explanation.surface: Someone weighs up taking a chemical to get stronger.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle means physical power, a synonym of strength.

clue.text: Each lock trimmed and arranged to show part of ear

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are put into a new order
trimmed means the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A hairdresser cuts and styles every lock to reveal the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trimmed' cuts K from LOCK, and 'arranged' shuffles EACH with LOC.
explanation.definitionFit: The cochlea is the spiral cavity of the inner ear.

clue.text: Unproductive, half-misguided assault

indicators.note: half the word is sent the wrong way, so its first two letters are turned round

parts.note: a raid is a sudden attack

explanation.surface: A partly bungled attack achieves nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-misguided' turns round the first half of RAID, RA becoming AR.
explanation.definitionFit: Arid land is dry and barren, so it yields nothing.

clue.text: Wild dogs captured by academic (Oxford mathematician)

indicators.note: captured by means the next pieces are held inside the academic

parts.note: a don is a university lecturer

indicators.note: wild means the letters run free into a new order

explanation.surface: Feral dogs are caught by a scholar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges 'dogs' into ODGS, and 'captured by' holds that inside the academic. Charles Dodgson was Lewis Carroll.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Dodgson taught mathematics at Christ Church and wrote as Lewis Carroll.

clue.text: Be aware: no time to lose heart

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters go, keeping only the first and last

explanation.surface: A warning that there is no time to get discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lose heart' strips the middle from TIME, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: To note something is to take notice of it, to be conscious of it.

clue.text: Novel result of striking redecoration?

definitions.meaning: a Sherlock Holmes book by Arthur Conan Doyle
a study is a room, and a room painted a vivid red is a striking makeover

explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's first Holmes book; read literally a den repainted bright red.
